problem: What molecular electronic evidence can explain differences in triplet sensitization among IR780, Cy1 and Cy2, and does it support their energetic compatibility with rubrene in chloroform?
facts: Source transient-absorption fitting yielded triplet quantum yields of7%,9% and23% for IR780,Cy1,Cy2 respectively. These are model-derived experimental summaries, not computed-state targets or exact uncertainties.
The sensitizers differ in more than heavy-atom identity; Cy1 and Cy2 are not isostructural iodine/selenium substitutions.
Rubrene mixtures emitted around557 nm under830 nm excitation. This observation does not establish a unique molecular sensitization mechanism.
scope: Use the complete IR780 (C36H44ClN2+), Cy1 (C34H38ClI2N2+) and Cy2 (C27H29N2O2Se2+) cation graphs and neutral rubrene (C42H28). The source molecular model excludes counterions. Solution context is chloroform; experimental upconversion mixtures were argon-saturated, with10 μM sensitizer and1.5 mM rubrene. Keep this measurement context distinct from an isolated-molecule calculation.
resource_facts: The platform supplies registered chemistry actions, native-software execution and selected Python runtimes. Inspect their actual capabilities and allocated resources. No specialist interface, license, cost or total compute budget is guaranteed by this task.
known_input_limits: Full raw transient spectra and fit covariance are not supplied; experimental yields are context and cannot support a new precise kinetic refit. Direct molecular SOC and heavy-element approximations need implementation-specific applicability checks.
